questions.prompt: We have two Software Engineer roles at Palantir for New Grads. Please confirm that you are interested in the Forward Deployed Software Engineer role as opposed to Software Engineer.
questions.draftAnswer: I am interested in the Forward Deployed Software Engineer role because I want to connect software implementation with a concrete operational problem. My strongest experience is in Python, retrieval evaluation and reliable agent workflows. In my document-search internship prototype, I owned evaluation scripts and citation checks; in Study Search, I own ingestion, evaluation and the local review interface. I would bring that habit of making outputs inspectable and failures reproducible to a customer-facing engineering team. I am completing my MS in June 2027 and would be available from July 2027. This is a fictional candidate response for a pre-submission course test.

questions.prompt: Give us three numbers that describe you — and tell us why.
questions.draftAnswer:
180: the synthetic retrieval questions I curated during my internship prototype. Building the questions and reference documents mattered as much as writing the retrieval code.

60: the fixed development questions used to compare retrieval changes. Recall@5 moved from 0.64 to 0.79 on that split; I keep that scope explicit rather than claiming held-out or production performance.

3: the people on my Agent Task Bench course team. I owned tool validation and failure analysis, and learned to describe my contribution separately from my teammates’ work.

All figures are fictional candidate fixture facts for a pre-submission test, not measured results for this course project.
